name: Fade Beater Demo
formation: 2-Man Shell vs Gun 12 Personnel Solo Left

summary.motive: Demonstrate why the classic red-zone fade fails against press-trail — the isolation throw offenses covet is exactly what this structure invites and erases.
summary.keyDefender: LCB playing outside-leverage press — his jam converts the fade into a footrace along a sideline he already owns
summary.whyItWorks: Outside leverage narrows the route before it develops, while the deep half erases anything that somehow clears the trail.
summary.failureMode: A clean inside-to-outside stack beating the jam in one move — then only the safety’s angle stands between the fade and six.

beats.title: 1. Why the Fade Tempts
beats.text: An isolated receiver with the end zone behind him is the throw every coordinator wants — but this island comes pre-loaded with an outside-leverage press corner.

beats.title: 2. The Jam Steals the Release
beats.text: A fade needs a clean stack from step one; the two-hand punch converts the release into a shoving match that kills the route’s spacing.

beats.title: 3. Trail Rides It to the Sideline
beats.text: With no room to stack, the receiver runs the fade alongside the corner, narrowing himself against the boundary he cannot escape.

beats.title: 4. Half Safety Erases the Shot
beats.text: The back-shoulder launch sails over both trail and receiver and out of bounds — the defense gambled nothing and lost nothing.

relations.tell: The corner is at 1 yard with pure outside leverage staring through the receiver — soft-squat Cover 2 sits at 7 yards with eyes on the QB.
